name: Mauna Kea
headline: baseToSummit
subtitle: Island of Hawai'i, USA
description: Mauna Kea is a volcano on the Island of Hawai'i and the highest peak in the state, reaching 4,207 m (13,803 ft) above sea level. Most of the mountain lies under the Pacific: the USGS says it extends about 6,000 m below sea level to the ocean floor, giving a total height of about 10,211 m from base to summit. Measured that way it is taller than Mount Everest, and its summit hosts a large group of astronomical observatories.

facts.text: USGS says Mauna Kea's total height from the ocean floor is considerably greater than the height of Mount Everest above sea level.
Mauna Kea is slightly taller than neighbouring Mauna Loa above sea level, but Mauna Loa's base is much deeper and it is far larger in volume.
The University of Hawai'i Institute for Astronomy says the summit sits above 40 percent of Earth's atmosphere, and it describes Mauna Kea as rising 9,750 m (32,000 ft) from the ocean floor.

caveats: Summit figures differ slightly between sources: the USGS Mauna Kea page gives 4,207 m (13,803 ft), while the USGS FAQ and the University of Hawai'i Institute for Astronomy use an older 4,205 m (13,796 ft).
Base-to-summit height depends on where the base is taken to be. USGS gives about 10,211 m; the University of Hawai'i Institute for Astronomy gives 9,750 m (32,000 ft).
The headline height is above sea level so it compares directly with other mountains; the base-to-summit figure is listed separately.
The mountain outline is illustrative; only its height is to scale.
